stories.title: U.S. senators call on NBA to reevaluate Rwanda partnership
stories.summary: Two U.S. senators called on the NBA to reevaluate a partnership with Rwanda and its dictator Paul Kagame, citing the American government's changing policy toward the small African nation.
stories.detailText: Two U.S. senators called on the NBA to reevaluate a partnership with Rwanda and its dictator Paul Kagame, citing the American government's changing policy toward the small African nation, which has been accused of widespread human rights abuses. In a letter sent Friday to commissioner Adam Silver, Sens. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., and Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., wrote that they are "increasingly alarmed by the NBA's deepening relationship with Rwanda" and said the league "risks becoming complicit in sportswashing," where governments or companies use sports to distract from human rights abuses, corruption and other activities. The senators said the partnership is "contrary to the spirit of American sports." In a statement to ESPN, NBA spokesman Mike Bass said, "We received the letter on Friday and are in the process of responding to it." The same senators wrote Silver two years ago in response to an ESPN article that detailed the NBA's embrace of Kagame , the country's leader since 1994. Rwanda, one of the poorest countries in the world, built a 10,000-seat arena in its capital of Kigali, and that facility has been central to the NBA's expansion into Africa. Kagame's government has been accused by the U.S., UK and other countries, as well as a string of human rights organizations, of abuses ranging from imprisonment, torture and murder of political opponents to the funding of child soldiers in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. Just last week, Robert Kabera, a former Rwandan soldier who became an outspoken critic of Kagame and had fled the country in 2020, was found beheaded in Uganda. Human rights organizations have called for an investigation into whether the killing was politically motivated. The NBA's position on its partnership with Rwanda, as expressed by NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum both to ESPN and then to the senators two years ago, is that the league has "[followed] the lead of the U.S. government as to where it is appropriate to engage in business around the world. "If American policies were to change regarding business activities in and relating to Rwanda ... our actions would of course change accordingly," Tatum wrote to the senators in 2024. The senators now say the policies of the U.S., UK and other European nations have "shifted markedly" toward Rwanda. The letter cited Rwanda's role in fomenting the conflict in the DRC, including through deployment of 18,000 troops and its command of the M23, a rebel group "which has summarily executed hundreds of civilians, committed mass rape, recruited child soldiers, and tortured civilians," the senators wrote. At the end of their letter, the senators asked the NBA to answer a series of questions, the first of which read: "What is the NBA's red line for accepting money from foreign governments that commit human rights abuses?" Kagame has said his country is using sports to bolster its economy and its place on the world stage. This month, Rwanda signed a 10-year deal to bring Formula 1 racing back to Africa, with the country expected to host its first race early in the next decade. A year ago, the NBA's LA Clippers and NFL's Los Angeles Rams announced multiyear deals in which the Rwanda government would pay the teams. "Visit Rwanda" -- the marketing slogan for the Rwanda Development Board -- became the exclusive jersey patch for the Clippers, while the slogan is advertised in the Rams' home, SoFi Stadium. The NBA launched a league in Africa in 2021 and its business there was valued at nearly $1 billion five years ago. Rwanda pays the NBA $6 million to $7 million per year to host some of the Basketball Africa League championships and display "Team Rwanda" on jerseys, as well as other marketing ties. Early last year, the DRC called on the NBA, Formula 1 and major international soccer clubs to end their multimillion-dollar partnerships with Rwanda. At the time, an F1 spokesman wrote in an email to ESPN: "We have been closely monitoring the developments relating to the DRC and Rwanda and continue to do so. We assess any potential request in detail and any future decisions would be based on the full information and what is in the best interests of our sport and our values." Months later, amid pressure from fans and media, Bayern Munich and Arsenal said they were ending their multimillion-dollar sponsorship deals with Rwanda.

stories.summary: Kessler never found his groove during the Lakers’ comeback victory on Sunday
stories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UT - OCTOBER 25: Walker Kessler #14 of the Los Angeles Lakers smiles during the game against the Utah Jazz on October 25, 2026 at Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Melissa Majchrzak/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images After averaging 24 points (84.6% shooting), 8.5 rebounds, 4.0 blocks and 1.5 steals through the first two games of the season, Walker Kessler struggled mightily during the Los Angeles Lakers’ comeback win Sunday against the Utah Jazz. In 28 minutes, he had two points (1-of-2 shooting) and seven rebounds, and committed four fouls. The matchup marked Kessler’s return to Utah, where he spent the first four years of his career before joining Los Angeles this summer. Afterward, Kessler admitted emotions may have played a role in his poor performance. “Obviously Utah was the first four years of my career. It’s a special place for me. Kind of jump started my career,” Kessler told reporters. “A lot of good memories, but definitely just let my emotions get the best of me and kind of hype myself up more than I usually do and kind of got too amped and then just couldn’t find the ball. Couldn’t find the rhythm. Just kind of was off. A couple fouls that were tough. A couple of blocks I usually just [get to]. One of those nights, but, fortunately, basketball is not a one-man sport. I’ve got really good teammates and I’m very thankful.” As Kessler labored through a lackluster outing, the Lakers’ star backcourt pairing led the charge. Luka Dončić dazzled with 52 points (17-of-30 shooting), 10 rebounds, eight assists and two steals while Austin Reaves continued his strong start to the year, dropping 29 points (7-of-12 shooting), four assists, two blocks and one steal. Matisse Thybulle added 11 points (3-of-7 beyond the arc), three steals and one block. “I think going to the game, I definitely let my emotions get the best of me. But you got to learn in those moments and move on,” Kessler told reporters. “But, yeah, I’m glad we got the win tonight. I’ve got a lot of thanks to give to my teammates. All of them. They all played their roles and did a great job even though it wasn’t my best night. So I really, really appreciated them.” Kessler will have a chance to bounce back Tuesday night at 8 p.m. when Los Angeles hosts the Portland Trail Blazers in a clash between undefeated teams. stories.title: NBA Stock Up, Stock Down Oct 26: Pistons, Rockets, Timberwolves climb while Heat, Knicks fall
stories.summary: Our weekly look at who is up and down in our NBA Power Rankings saw a lot of dramatic movement.
stories.detailText: The first few weeks of the season always see dramatic moves in the NBA Power Rankings. Some teams are better than we thought, others are worse, but mostly it's small sample size theater — if the Knicks dropped three straight games in January, the NBA would just shrug. Still, we have a fair amount of ground to cover in our first edition of Stock Up, Stock Down, looking at the teams that are the most dramatic risers and fallers in the NBC Sports NBA Power Rankings . Here are the teams to keep an eye on. Stock up • The Oklahoma City Thunder move up two spots to take over No. 1, although the gruesome leg injury to Jalen Williams has put a dark cloud over any celebrations of the team's fast start. • The Detroit Pistons and Houston Rockets each move up four spots to take over the No. 2 and No. 3 spots in the power rankings. • The Minnesota Timberwolves jumped up seven spots from outside the top-10 to No. 4. We knew their LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards offense would be good, but the defense has been near the league's best to start the season. • The Toronto Raptors jumped up seven spots to be No. 7 in this week's rankings, another team with an elite defense — when Kawhi Leonard is healthy. • The Memphis Grizzlies jumped up eight spots to No. 17 after an unexpected 3-0 start, behind the equally surprising but unstoppable Ty Jerome, who is averaging 34.7 points a game so far. • Shout out to the Charlotte Hornets , which climbed seven spots up to No. 19 behind a fast start from Brandon Miller, while still missing some key players (such as Kon Knueppel). Stock Down • Nobody's stock fell faster than the New York Knicks, who fell a dozen spots from No. 1 all the way down to 13th. Losing to East contenders such as Philadelphia and Boston is one thing, but losing to a Banchero-less Orlando is another. Physicality and shooting seem to have gone missing in NYC, but nobody there is panicking. Yet. • The winless Miami Heat fell 10 spots down to 23rd in the latest power rankings. The Heat have trailed by at least 20 points in every game, and the defense that was supposed to anchor them is bottom-five in the league. There might be a little panic in South Beach. • The San Antonio Spurs fell six spots to No. 8, and Victor Wembanyama has looked almost human to start the season. Expect that to change.

stories.title: Luka Doncic sends savage response to longtime critic after 52-point explosion
stories.summary: Luka Dončić dropped 52 points in a Los Angeles Lakers win then offered a swift response to critic Kendrick Perkins.
stories.detailText: Luka Dončić has not needed to shake off any rust this season. The superstar guard produced a staggering 52-point performance in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 132-123 win over the Utah Jazz on Sunday night. Dončić’s 34.3 points per game is second-highest in the league and a key reason why the Lakers are undefeated to this point in the season. Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers hushes the crowd after sinking a three-pointer against the Utah Jazz during the second half of a game at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images One of Dončić’s biggest critics over the years has been Kendrick Perkins . The former NBA forward called Dončić out for having missed time during the playoffs with an injury last season and even defended the Dallas Mavericks’ decision to trade Luka in 2025 because he didn’t believe Dončić was prepared to lead a team to a NBA championship. Kendrick Perkins attends the Ruffles NBA All-Star Celebrity Game during the 2022 NBA All-Star Weekend at Wolstein Center on Friday, Feb. 18, 2022, in Cleveland. Getty Images But even Perkins couldn’t deny Dončić’s dominance on Sunday, as he made an X post in the wake of Los Angeles’ win against Utah that read, “Luka with a cool 52 and 10 on the lord’s day.”. Dončić responded to this, writing, “. ” Luka Dončić and Kendrick Perkins’ social media exchange after Dončić scored 52 points in a Los Angeles Lakers win. (X/@KendrickPerkins). Dončić’s response has over 600,000 views in about 13 hours. This savage response suggests Dončić has seen what Perkins has said in the past and was eager to show that he sees Perkins’ praise as well. Even Perkins has to admit that Dončić appears to be in his prime right now. The Lakers will look to remain undefeated on Tuesday against the Trailblazers in Los Angeles.

teamStories.summary: Steady starter to an All-Star lock? Top-10 talent to an MVP? Breakout seasons take many forms in the NBA. Ben Golliver identifies 30 players primed to take the next step.
teamStories.detailText: Career progression can take many forms in the NBA: cracking the starting lineup, earning a first All-Star selection or making the leap into the MVP conversation, to name a few. Let's survey which players are primed for breakout campaigns by first acknowledging that "breakout" can have very different meanings depending on a player's talent and experience. The 30 players listed below are all primed to take the next step in 2026-27 and have been sorted into tiers based on their current credentials and the circumstances contributing to their projected improvement. Jump to a tier: Breakouts to: MVP | Superstar | All-Star | Starter Breakout picks featuring: Recent trades | Rookies Tier 1: First MVP? Who makes the cut: Multitime All-Stars who could conceivably break through to their first MVP in 2026-27. Victor Wembanyama , Spurs Last season, Wembanyama finished third in MVP voting and led the Spurs to the Finals during his age-22 campaign, cementing his status as the NBA's top blue-chip prospect since LeBron James . After proving he could captain an elite defense and survive the Western Conference's playoff gauntlet, the French center must refine his isolation scoring game and become a more dependable closer to claim the "Best in the World" throne. Given his rapid improvement during his first three seasons, those developments feel like a matter of "when," not "if." Luka Doncic , Lakers The Lakers have fully recalibrated around the 27-year-old Doncic, who is perennially one of the league's top scorers and passers. Doncic has never finished higher than third in MVP voting, but his candidacy should benefit from a new-look supporting cast that's tailored to his strengths and an expected spike in usage after James' offseason departure. Doncic's health looms as a potential drawback: His best chance to win MVP relies on the Lakers finishing with 50-plus wins, a bar they won't clear if he misses significant time. Cade Cunningham , Pistons The low-key Cunningham might not generate as much buzz as some of his contemporaries, but he checks all the boxes for aspiring MVPs by putting up big numbers, driving wins and serving as the reliable face of a Finals contender. The 2021 No. 1 pick finished fifth in MVP voting last season after leading Detroit to 60 wins and the East's No. 1 seed. If the Pistons defy their preseason doubters and finish in the conference's top tier again, the 25-year-old Cunningham will almost certainly show up on more ballots this time around. Anthony Edwards , Timberwolves Similar to Wembanyama and Cunningham, Edwards is another former No. 1 pick on the ascent. The 25-year-old shooting guard hasn't yet finished in the top five for MVP voting, but he has led the Timberwolves on multiple deep postseason runs and is flanked by a potent new sidekick in LaMelo Ball . Though Edwards' advanced statistics often leave something to be desired compared to past MVP winners, he has a decent chance to win his first scoring title and arguably already leads the league in charisma. Tyrese Maxey , 76ers Maxey is a model of continual improvement: His scoring average increased from year to year in each of his first six seasons, and he followed his first All-Star selection in 2024 with his first All-NBA nod in 2026. Philadelphia's lightning-quick guard has mastered his scoring craft, and he's bound to get more national attention playing alongside James and Jaylen Brown on the souped-up 76ers. Though Dwyane Wade, Kyrie Irving and Anthony Davis never generated much traction as MVP candidates while playing in James' shadow, the star dynamic is different in Philadelphia given that Maxey is 25 and James is 41. Tier 2: All-Star to superstar? Who makes the cut: Players with at least one All-Star selection who could vault into the top-15 conversation by season's end. Scottie Barnes , Raptors To date, the 25-year-old Barnes hasn't really functioned as a prototypical alpha scorer or proven to be a knockdown perimeter shooter. That's OK because the Raptors' forward is a very good offensive player, an exceptional defender and a strong fit alongside Kawhi Leonard . Though Barnes' winning qualities might have been masked during Toronto's rebuilding years, they should be on full display now that the Raptors expect to make playoff progress with Leonard in the fold. His positional versatility on defense, his comfort playing on and off the ball, and his imposing physicality are rarely found in a player. Chet Holmgren , Thunder Now is a good time to buy low on the 24-year-old Holmgren, whose poor showing against Wembanyama's Spurs in the conference finals prompted plenty of social media criticism. The 2022 No. 2 pick is arguably the league's best rim protector other than Wembanyama, and he's a skilled complementary scorer who can finish inside over smaller defenders and step out beyond the arc to beat traditional big men with his jumper. Oklahoma City's deep bench has given Holmgren the luxury of playing under 30 minutes per game throughout his career, but he's a prime candidate to pick up the offensive slack after Jalen Williams ' serious ankle injury. Jalen Johnson , Hawks Johnson emerged as a fantasy basketball superstar last season thanks to his eye-popping production. In reality, he still has some work to do. Though the 24-year-old forward received the keys to Atlanta's offense after Trae Young 's departure, the Hawks were left scrambling for answers when he faltered during the playoffs. A little patience was in order, as Johnson barely played as a rookie and missed most of the 2024-25 season because of injury. Now, his reputation is set to soar if he can lead a deep and talented Hawks team on a real playoff run. Tier 3: Standout to All-Star? Who makes the cut: Big names aspiring for their first All-Star selection. Cooper Flagg , Mavericks All signs point up for the 2026 Rookie of the Year, back for his second season with a new coach in Dusty May and a healthy co-star in Irving. Flagg, 19, led Dallas in points, rebounds, assists and steals last season, flashing future MVP potential despite his team's struggles. With James and Leonard joining Eastern Conference teams this summer, a spot could open for Flagg in the Western Conference All-Star selection process. Of course, that's assuming the shoulder injury he suffered Friday doesn't linger. Austin Reaves , Lakers After going undrafted in 2021, Reaves cashed in on years of steady, purposeful development by signing a four-year, $180 million extension this summer. Reaves has become everything the Lakers could want in a No. 2 option: He can create shots off the dribble, get to the free throw line, score effectively when off the ball and pass well enough to function as a lead or secondary playmaker. And the 28-year-old also has a knack for establishing strong interpersonal relationships with stars such as James and Doncic. Amen Thompson , Rockets Thompson, 23, was thrown into playmaking duties last season as Houston sought to cope with veteran guard Fred VanVleet 's knee injury. Though Thompson responded with a productive campaign that netted him a five-year, $208 million contract extension, he appears set up for a more efficient and stable role now that VanVleet's back in the lineup as an organizer. Whether or not Thompson ever develops a reliable 3-point shot, he has All-Star tools thanks to his elite quickness, strength, power and agility. The 6-7 forward's ability to get into the paint, finish at the rim and function as a secondary distributor separates him from the average defensive specialist. Stephon Castle , Spurs Castle, 21, has probably supplanted De'Aaron Fox as the most likely Spurs player besides Wembanyama to get an All-Star nod. The 2024 No. 4 pick has emerged as the best player in his draft class thanks to his relentless dribble drives and physical perimeter defense. Castle isn't a natural point guard and has struggled with turnovers, but he's well-situated in San Antonio as a secondary creator. Dylan Harper , Spurs Harper was so electric as a super substitute during San Antonio's 2026 Finals run that he forced his way into the Spurs' starting lineup. The 20-year-old guard is a crafty finisher with excellent body control, the ability to seamlessly change speeds and a fearlessness well beyond his years. The 2025 No. 2 pick entered the season as a popular Most Improved Player candidate, and his All-Star chances will likely be shaped by how coach Mitch Johnson manages his guard-heavy rotation. Jaden McDaniels , Timberwolves Though McDaniels has been a favorite of Edwards and Timberwolves fans for years, he's positioned for greater individual recognition nationally after the departures of Julius Randle and Naz Reid this summer. As part of Minnesota's brash and exciting new identity, the 26-year-old forward is a strong fit alongside Edwards and Ball. Long known for his physical and versatile defending, McDaniels has blossomed into a reliable third scorer during his seven-year tenure with the Timberwolves. Brandon Miller , Hornets Miller has taken the reins as Charlotte's franchise player after Ball's offseason trade. The 2023 No. 2 pick didn't quite display superstar potential during his first three seasons, but his reliable scoring and high-volume 3-point shooting earned him a five-year, $209 million extension earlier this month. The next steps for the 23-year-old forward are clear: put more pressure on the rim, regularly get to the free throw line and help with the playmaking duties in Ball's absence. Tier 4: Second unit to starter? Who makes the cut: Former backups looking to make an impact in the starting lineup. Ty Jerome , Grizzlies Jerome, a journeyman who was a finalist for 2025 Sixth Man of the Year with the Cleveland Cavaliers , was bumped up into the Grizzlies' starting lineup last season before injuries limited him to 15 games. The 29-year-old guard relished his return by scoring a career-high 45 points in Memphis' season-opening win over the Utah Jazz . His controlled, efficient scoring and 3-point range make him a capable floor general for the Grizzlies' rebuilding effort. Naz Reid, Hornets Reid, 27, was a perennial Sixth Man of the Year candidate for the Timberwolves, but an offseason trade to the Hornets has positioned him as a frontcourt starter and veteran leader. The undrafted big man has the chops as a scorer, rebounder and defender to handle the promotion. If things go as planned, Reid will easily average career highs in points and 3-point attempts in Charlotte's perimeter-oriented offense. Cason Wallace , Thunder Wallace, 22, is the Thunder's designated Luguentz Dort replacement: a relentless perimeter defender who balances OKC's starting backcourt alongside two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander . Though Wallace doesn't have Dort's broad frame, he regularly blows up possessions with his incredible hands and on-ball instincts. To live up to his new five-year, $139 million contract, Wallace must show growth as a ballhandling threat and outside shooter. Khaman Maluach , Suns Maluach emerged as Phoenix's starting center for opening night after Mark Williams underwent shoulder surgery in September. The 20-year-old big man is a crucial piece for the Suns' long-term future given his 7-1 frame and potential to develop into a rim-protecting stretch 5. Whether or not Maluach maintains his starting spot, Phoenix must ensure he receives a healthy amount of playing time throughout his second season. The Duke product logged a paltry 411 minutes as a rookie, making him the only 2025 top 10 pick to play fewer than 1,200 minutes last season. Tier 5: New team, new results? Who makes the cut: players who found greener pastures thanks to recent trades. Walker Kessler , Lakers Kessler is now in center nirvana after a summer sign-and-trade sent him from the Jazz to the Lakers, and he will continue enjoying a steady stream of lobs from Doncic and Reaves. The 25-year-old Kessler should even draw consideration for USA Basketball's 2028 Olympic team due to his paint finishing and interior defensive presence. Ivica Zubac , Pacers After thriving as a pick-and-roll partner with James Harden on the LA Clippers in years past, Zubac should occupy a similar role on Tyrese Haliburton 's Pacers. Though the 29-year-old center has never made an All-Star team, he could generate some buzz if he stacks up double-doubles in Indiana. Darius Garland , Clippers Garland, 26, had to keep everyone involved and defer to No. 1 option Donovan Mitchell during the latter stages of his Cavaliers tenure, but a move to the rebuilding Clippers has thrust him into a score-first role. A lack of size has held back Garland in the playoffs, but he possesses enough shot-creation ability, quickness and range to function as a three-level scorer while the Clippers wait for several key players to get healthy. Jared McCain , Thunder Since arriving from the 76ers in a February trade, the 22-year-old McCain has been a strong answer to the Thunder's biggest weakness in recent years: inconsistent outside shooting. When Oklahoma City's half-court offense bogs down, McCain has a knack for injecting energy and flow with his deadeye shooting. Don't be surprised if there's a Sixth Man of the Year award in his future. Peyton Watson , Cavaliers Watson had to leave the Nuggets for the Cavaliers in a summer sign-and-trade to secure his new four-year, $88 million contract, and the 24-year-old forward cleanly fills what was the biggest hole in Cleveland's starting lineup. Though his offensive usage could take a hit given the Cavaliers' many scoring threats, he will have every opportunity to showcase his value as a perimeter defender for a veteran team with Finals aspirations. Zaccharie Risacher , Mavericks Expectations should be modest for Risacher, the 2024 No. 1 pick who lasted just two seasons in Atlanta. But the 21-year-old French forward landed with a retooling Mavericks organization that's seemingly motivated to fashion him into a reliable rotation player. Risacher lacks the dynamic athleticism to be a star, but he could still enjoy a lucrative career if he can pivot into a 3-and-D contributor. Tier 6: Impact rookies Who makes the cut: 2026 lottery picks should be able to shine from day one. Cameron Boozer , Grizzlies Boozer, 19, should be thrilled he landed on a roster that boasts a solid lead guard in Jerome to run the offense and multiple traditional centers to protect the 6-10 power forward from wear and tear. As Boozer tries to lead the rebuilding Grizzlies back to respectability, he has a head start on his fellow 2026 lottery picks when it comes to role definition and roster structure. That could pay off with a Rookie of the Year award. AJ Dybantsa , Wizards The 19-year-old Dybantsa was selected No. 1 because he is a pro-ready scorer who can get downhill and draw contact. Though the Wizards will need to juggle some competing interests as they mesh veteran stars Anthony Davis and Trae Young with a younger core led by Dybantsa, the former BYU star has the highest ceiling of any Washington prospect since 2010 No. 1 pick John Wall. Caleb Wilson , Bulls Wilson, 20, looks headed for a roller coaster rookie season with the dreadful Bulls: After posting a minus-45 in his NBA debut against the Raptors, he responded with 30 points and 14 rebounds in a strong showing against the Wizards a few nights later. As a 6-10 forward who plays well above the rim on both ends and can operate as a perimeter playmaker, Wilson has a strong case as his draft class' most tantalizing prospect. Darryn Peterson , Jazz Peterson, 19, can ease into life as Utah's starting two guard because he's surrounded by proven scorers in Keyonte George , Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr . Even so, the Jazz will want to see the second pick assert himself for stretches as an off-the-dribble creator and shotmaker. Peterson proved he could get hot in a hurry at Kansas despite an injury-plagued freshman season. Yaxel Lendeborg , Warriors The 24-year-old Lendeborg is older and more physically developed than the typical rookie, which is good news for the reeling Warriors. With Jimmy Butler III , Kristaps Porzingis and other key contributors out to start the season, the 6-9 Lendeborg has stepped into the starting lineup and made an immediate impact as a secondary scorer and on-ball defender. If Lendeborg sustains his production in a starting role all season, will the No. 11 pick unexpectedly beat out his teenage classmates for Rookie of the Year?

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Welcome to Week in Review: a Monday feature that looks back at the week that was for the San Antonio Spurs , takes a look at the week ahead, and more. Enjoy! Week 1: 1-2 (1-2, 9th in West ) 104-116 loss vs. Oklahoma City Thunder It wasn’t the season opener the Spurs had hoped for. With the Thunder out for revenge for the Western Conference Finals and red hot from three in the first half, the lethargic Spurs went ice cold in the second quarter to fall behind by 26 points and, despite an admirable effort in the second half, couldn’t rally all the way back. On a side note, keep Jalen Williams in your thoughts after he suffered a brutal looking leg injury last night (I don’t recommend making the same mistake as me and watching it). Assuming it’s as bad as it looks, he’s more than likely out for the season and faces an even harder road back. 110-114 loss vs. Houston Rockets (in Austin) The Spurs looked better in their second game as they continued to shake off the rust and find some rhythm, but it still wasn’t enough against a healthy Rockets squad that finally has a true point guard. Alperen Sengun was unstoppable down low no matter who guarded him, and Amen Thompson blocked Victor Wembanyama’s game tying attempt for the heart-breaking loss. 106-122 win at Dallas Mavericks The Spurs finally got their first win of the season against a depleted Mavs team that was missing Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving, among others. While nothing special, the Spurs’ starters did their jobs and put the opponent away with a few timely runs, and we even got to see what Tarris Reed could bring to the table in rotation minutes. Power Rankings John Schuhmann, NBA.com — 6 (last week: 1) OffRtg: 110.5 (14) DefRtg: 111.3 (14) NetRtg: -0.7 (14) A season with big expectations got off to a rough start for Victor Wembanyama (1-for-13 against the Thunder) and the Spurs. After losing to Oklahoma City and Houston, they trailed the shorthanded Mavs (no Kyrie Irving or Cooper Flagg) late in the third quarter on Saturday before pulling away in the final 13 minutes. Two takeaways 1. The Spurs’ new starting lineup played limited minutes ( just 9.4 per game ) and the results were mixed. It outscored the Thunder by 10 points on Tuesday, but scored an anemic 30 points on 45 offensive possessions ( 67 per 100 ) against the Rockets and Mavs over the weekend. The offense was at its best with last season’s starter (Julian Champagnie) on the floor. 2. Victor Wembanyama has struggled with his jump shot. Combining preseason and Week 1 , he’s shot 2-for-11 from mid-range and 5-for-28 from beyond the arc. But the Spurs have allowed less than a point per possession with him on the floor, while allowing 133 per 100 with him on the bench. Coming up: The Spurs’ win in Dallas over the weekend was the start of what seems like a pretty soft, 12-game stretch of schedule that should have them at or near the top of the West in mid-November. Minnesota is the toughest opponent on that stretch, but the Spurs will have a rest advantage when they host the Wolves on Saturday. Law Murray, The Athletic — 12 (last week: 5) Opening week question: Do De’Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle complement one another well enough? Defensively, the trio has been fine — it helps to have Victor Wembanyama back there. But these three are only starting together because that’s the team Mitch Johnson has to manage this year. Last year, Johnson could bring the second pick of the draft (Harper) off the bench, have Fox minimize his touches and play primarily through Castle while Wembanyama enjoyed his ascent to MVP finalist. This year, the Spurs are letting their guard trio dominate the ball. San Antonio is shooting only 41.5 percent from the field and 28.1 percent from 3. Kurt Helin, NBC Sports — 8 (last week: 2) Through three games, the jury is still out on starting the three guards together — De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper — with the group posting a +1.4 net rating when on the court together. With that trio, the defense has been spectacular, but the offense has struggled (granted, on an exceedingly small sample). One issue with starting the three-guard lineup is that the Spurs now lack the bench punch Harper brought last season. It’s wild to say it, but the bigger problem for the Spurs — especially against the Thunder on opening night — was Victor Wembanyama. Against OKC, he held the ball too long, which disrupted the three-guard offense’s flow. Wemby shot 1-of-13 in the opener, partly because the Thunder are an elite defensive team, collapsed on him, and have three seven-footers to throw at him. In the Spurs’ second game against Houston, Wemby had a much better first half but struggled after halftime, then against Dallas he looked more like himself. The Spurs need that version of Wemby. Brett Siegel, Clutch Points — 9 (last week: 4) This was an unprecedented start for the defending Western Conference champions. While falling to the Thunder in the first game of the season wasn’t all that shocking, losing to the Rockets in a game they never really controlled was. Not only is Victor Wembanyama struggling to find his shot early on, but the Spurs are still trying to figure out what their three-guard approach looks like on a nightly basis with De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, and Dylan Harper. Getting Tobias Harris back on the floor from his calf injury will be important for this team, especially since he brings extra rebounding and secondary scoring. Nonetheless, this team’s success revolves around Wembanyama’s production, which was lackluster during the first week of the season. stories.title: Ex-Cowboy Dez Bryant calls out police investigation after he's cited for assault
stories.summary: Dez Bryant is calling for a thorough investigation by the Southlake Police Department of an incident that resulted in him receiving a citation for assault.
stories.detailText: Former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant is calling for a thorough investigation by the Southlake (Texas) Police Department of an incident on Sunday that resulted in him receiving a citation for assault. Bryant, 37, told Outkick that he confronted two drivers in a parking lot of a Mexican restaurant after they allegedly cut him off in traffic Sunday. He told the media outlet that he wanted to tell them to drive safer, but when an argument ensued with one of the men, who Bryant described as a young adult, that driver insinuated that "he'll shoot me or whatever." Bryant told Outkick that he told the man that if he pulled out a gun, "you better use it because if you don't, I'm going to do something to you." Bryant, however, said the man never pulled out a weapon and instead took out his cell phone to record him. Bryant proceeded to knock the phone out of the man's hand. The man then called police, which Bryant said he encouraged because he believed they would investigate the alleged threat against him. When police arrived, an officer ordered all three men to the ground at gunpoint and put them in handcuffs. Bryant's girlfriend later came to the scene with his two daughters and recorded the incident. Bryant provided the video to Outkick. "I was really more so concerned about my children, you know, looking at their dad, you know, being on the ground with a gun pointed at me," Bryant told Outkick. Southlake police spokesperson Capt. Blas Hernandez said in a news release, which was obtained by ESPN, that officers arrived to the scene with their weapons drawn because 911 calls indicated there was "a possible weapon" at the scene. He said that the officers' approach to the scene was a "precaution to address any potential threats and ensure the safety of everyone at the scene." "No firearms were recovered at the scene," Hernandez said. Bryant told Outkick that officers only viewed the man's recording and didn't review surveillance footage, including from the traffic incident. He told Outkick that only he received a citation from police. According to an online record, Bryant was cited for assault by contact with an initial hearing set for Nov. 20. The citation carries a fine of $367. Bryant called the police investigation "very one-sided" and said one officer told him that he should be "the bigger person." He said he reached out to Outkick because, "my reputation mean everything to me." "Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody with respect," he said, when asked by Outkick what he wants from police. "Do your due diligence on what's actually going on." Bryant, who last played in the NFL in 2020, was a three-time Pro Bowl selection in his career. He still ranks first all-time in Cowboys franchise history in touchdown receptions (73), fourth in receptions (531) and sixth in receiving yards (7,459).

stories.title: Ravens' Jesse Minter optimistic QB Lamar Jackson can return vs. Bills
stories.summary: Ravens coach Jesse Minter expressed optimism Monday that quarterback Lamar Jackson could be available for Sunday's game against the Bills.
stories.detailText: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens coach Jesse Minter expressed optimism about quarterback Lamar Jackson 's availability this week but was not definitive on whether the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will start in Sunday's critical game at the Buffalo Bills . Jackson has missed the past three games with a high ankle sprain, including Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals . "I think he was able to get in a little bit of work obviously towards the end of last week," Minter said Monday. "And so I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday." Jackson seemed to be trending toward playing last week when he was a limited participant in every practice. Then, a day after being listed as questionable, Jackson was ruled out by Baltimore. Minter declined to confirm a report on the CBS game broadcast that Jackson woke up Saturday with increased swelling in his injured left ankle, which led to him being scratched. "So look, if he's able to play -- that's healthy enough to play and play the way that obviously we feel like he needs to play -- then he will play," Minter said. The Ravens (4-3) have struggled with fill-in starting quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley , losing two straight games to fall to last place in the AFC North. Without Jackson the past three weeks, the Ravens have averaged 17.7 points (24th in the NFL) and 328.3 yards (20th). Minter said he doesn't want to blame the offense's inconsistencies on Jackson not playing. "Lamar's 1 of 1, right? Two-time MVP, obviously a high-caliber player, but I just don't like the built-in excuse of why things are going a certain way," Minter said. "So while we know the caliber of player Lamar is and the numbers when he's out there versus when he's not, we understand all that. That's why he's who he is and why he's won the awards that he's won, but we can still operate better in those times where we don't have him for sure."

stories.title: A 16-game international week was never a possibility during 2020 CBA talks
stories.summary: On Sunday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claimed that, during the 2020 Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations, a discussion was had regarding the possibility of a full-blown "international week."

With all 32 teams playing in foreign countries on the same weekend. It sounded odd, and impractical. As best we can tell, it was never a serious consideration during the 2020 CBA talks — if it was even a consideration at all. While it's possible that the league chose 17 regular-season games over the ability to stage up to 16 annual international games, there was never a specific plan to play all 16 international games in the same week . It's borderline ludicrous on it's face. No games in any U.S. stadiums? Sixteen games played all over the world? With a Thursday night game, 14 on Sunday, and one on Monday night? It would be a logistical nightmare for the NFL, which would be staging a full slate of games in foreign soil in the same four-day window. The goal was, and still is, to turn the European games into a TV package, with multiple games starting at 9:30 a.m. ET. Emptying the international tank on one and only one weekend would make no sense. And there's no way the NFL would have accepted 16 international games plus two byes. The league experimented with two byes in 1993, and the networks hated it. A second bye extends the season, but it dilutes the number of games played in plenty of weeks with byes. In 1993, eight of 28 teams were off in Week 3, Week 4, Week 6, and Week 8. Six teams were off in Week 6, Week 11, and Week 13. Four teams were off in Week 10. And two teams were off in Week 12. While two byes may be needed to sell an 18-game season to the players, the league wouldn't have added a second bye to a 16-game season. (Indeed, it didn't add a second bye to a 17-game season.) More importantly, and despite Rodgers's claim, a full-league international week never was (and never will be) a realistic possibility.

stories.title: Andrew Berry: We're excited to keep Maliek Collins in Cleveland
stories.summary: The 5-3 Browns have another reason to celebrate on Monday.
stories.detailText: The 5-3 Browns have another reason to celebrate on Monday. Cleveland announced that defensive tackle Maliek Colins has signed his two-year contract extension with the club. The deal was agreed to over the weekend . "Since we signed Maliek in the 2025 offseason, he has been a disruptive player in the middle of our defense and one of the top interior pass rushers in football ," Browns General Manager Andrew Berry said in a statement. "His non-stop motor, selflessness and endless pass rush arsenal make him a perfect fit for our attack-style defense. As much as he has contributed to our defensive success on the field, the things he does behind the scenes are just as impactful. “For the past two years, Maliek has been THE veteran, stabilizing presence in the meeting rooms, on the practice field and in the facility. His impact on our young defensive line's growth can't be overstated. We're excited to keep Maliek in Cleveland for several more years.” Collins registered a career-high 6.5 sacks in 12 games with the Browns last season. In seven games so far this year, he’s tallied 3.5 sacks, six tackles for loss, and eight QB hits. A third-round pick in 2016, Collins has tallied 40.5 career sacks for the Cowboys, Raiders, Texans, 49ers, and Browns.

stories.summary: The Browns activated quarterback Dillon Gabriel off injured reserve Monday, giving the team four passers on the 53-man roster.
stories.detailText: BEREA, Ohio -- The Cleveland Browns activated quarterback Dillon Gabriel off injured reserve Monday, giving the team four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster. Gabriel, a 2025 third-round pick, was placed on IR with a back injury at the roster cutdown deadline in late August. He was designated to return to practice Oct. 6 and will now join Deshaun Watson , Shedeur Sanders and rookie Taylen Green on the active roster. Gabriel, who played in 10 career games with six starts as a rookie, has completed 110 of 185 passes for 937 yards with seven touchdowns. Watson, who won the quarterback competition in training camp, has started the first seven games for the AFC North-leading Browns (5-2), while Sanders has served as the backup. Green, a sixth-round pick, has been the emergency QB on game days.

stories.title: Steelers Week 7 grades in win over Saints
stories.summary: Steelers grades from Week 7 win over Saints.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are 5-2 after a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris. As always, Joey Bray and I are here to give your weekly grades, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers continues to be efficient while adding a pinch of explosiveness that lifts the Steelers’ offense. His best play of the day came on a 3rd-and-14 where he escaped pressure from the pocket, ran to his left, and uncorked a moon ball to DK Metcalf, who hauled it in for a gain of 51 inside the five yard-line. Plus, the eight-yard scramble to end the game was as clutch as it comes from a quarterback who has spent six presidential terms making clutch plays. It wasn’t an extraordinary performance, but it was a good overall showing from Rodgers. Grade: B+ Joey Bray : It wasn’t Rodgers’ most impressive stat line this season, but his 30 passing attempts were the fewest of the season. The Steelers controlled the clock with their running game and felt in control the entire time. Rodgers maneuvered the pocket better this game than he has all season, highlighted by an 8-yard run on third down late in the contest that helped the Steelers run the clock out. Rodgers continues to put the Steelers offense in positions to win. Grade: C RB Jaylen Warren Jarrett Bailey: Warren’s emergence as a legitimate top five running back has been so fun to watch in real time. The Steelers made it clear that he would be the focal point of the offense on the first drive, as he racked up 43 yards on the opening series and finished with 101 on the ground and 36 as a receiver. He continues to make a strong potential All-Pro case for himself as the Steelers continue to ride him to victories: Grade: A Joey Bray: According to Matt Williamson , Jaylen Warren is the first running back to have 550+ rushing yards and 250+ receiving yards in his first seven games in a season since Christian McCaffrey in 2019. Warren posted over 100 scrimmage yards in the first half on Sunday, and continues to be the most dynamic and effective player on the Steelers offense. Grade: A+ RB Rico Dowdle Jarrett Bailey : The Steelers have found the right balance of carries for Warren and Dowdle. Warren had 18 carries, Dowdle had nine for 41 yards and added 45 yards as a receiver. This balance of working Dowdle in to get touches while Warren remains the clear cut No. 1 is the best way for Pittsburgh to find success in its backfield. This is the second straight game that Dowdle has given them some juice in this role. Grade: B Joey Bray: Put some respect on Rico Dowdle’s name. Since he has returned from injury, Dowdle has been a great complement to Jaylen Warren. The efficiency has also drastically improved for Dowdle, who averaged 4.6 yards per carry on Sunday, while also hauling in six passes. Dowdle and Warren are becoming the one-two punch that Steelers fans were hoping they would be at the start of the season. Grade: B Offense Jarrett Bailey: There were a lot of things to like about the way the offense performed. Offensive line wise, it was maybe the best game the Steelers had all year, especially when it came to run blocking. Yes, Chase Young made a couple plays, but Rodgers was tied for the fifth-fewest pressures faced in Week 7. However, there was plenty to dislike. The fade routes to DK Metcalf should be burnt with fire and never called again, especially in the red zone on third down. Those are almost certainly Rodgers’ doing, and they need to end immediately. Finishing drives as a whole needs to be something that gets better, as well. The Steelers had four red zone trips and only turned one of them into a touchdown. 16 points isn’t going to be enough against the great teams in the league. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: My biggest complaint from yesterday would be about the Steelers struggling to finish drives and having to settle for field goals. It seems like small potatoes since they won, but Aaron Rodgers’ visible frustration on the sidelines in the fourth quarter after having to settle for a field goal was notable. The playcalling in plus territory was particularly questionable yesterday. With plenty of quality teams and divisional opponents in the second half of their schedule, the offense will have to be better and turn some of those field goals into touchdowns even if it didn’t end up mattering yesterday. Grade: C EDGE T.J Watt Jarrett Bailey: Watt has officially re-emerged as an elite edge rusher. He had another sack on Sunday, and was robbed of the trifecta of a sack,s trip, and recovery despite the ball clearly moving when he sacked Tyler Shough. Regardless, he is now fourth in the league in sacks and continues to look like his former self. Grade: A Joey Bray: The Steelers’ star defender was probably robbed of a strip-sack of Saints quarterback Tyler Shough. Although the strip was called back, Watt brought his sack total to 5.5 on the season. The edge rusher rotation in the Steelers’ defense this season has seemed to keep Watt fresh, as he has returned to being someone who can be a double digit sack guy, which he is well on pace to be again this season. Nobody has forced more strip sacks since 2017 than Watt, and he continues to prove he can change the game in the blink of an eye. Grade: A LB Patrick Queen Jarrett Bailey: Queen was awesome on Sunday in what was one of his best games as a Steeler. He had 10 tackles and seven impact plays, per Sumer Sports. The only linebacker with more such plays was Blake Cashman of the Minnesota Vikings. For a guy that gets more scrutiny from Steelers fans than any other player, it was good to see him play so well. I’ll throw in a hat tip to Payton Wilson, as well, who had the interception that swung the game. Good day for the Steelers’ linebacker duo. Grade: A Joey Bray: All things considered, this was one of the best games that Patrick Queen has played as a Steeler. Yes, the dropped pick was tough, but it’s hard for me to harp on linebackers dropping interceptions. Especially with the way Queen responded, as he led the team in tackles and came up with a huge sack in which he made a great move to get by the Saints’ offensive line. Queen was around the ball a lot yesterday and made several phenomenal plays. Grade: A+ Defense Jarrett Bailey: The defense has allowed just three touchdowns over their last three games, and have allowed just one second-half touchdown this entire season. Allowing just 18 yards on 17 carries is absurd at any level, and Pittsburgh’s run defense has been the best in the league over the last three weeks. There are things that need cleaned up, specifically the third down success rate for the Saints (6-of-12), but limiting New Orleans to under five yards per play is something they can hang their hat on. If they can sustain this high-level of play, they can beat anyone. Grade: A Joey Bray: Once again, the zone defense was frustrating to watch as Tyler Shough went 30/38 passing in the contest. Many online have dubbed the Steelers defense as the first “bend don’t break” defense in history. The secondary is going to continue to be an issue until a serious corner is added, which may very well not happen anytime this season. I think Graham deserves a lot of credit for having a great defensive game plan that held New Orleans to just 10 points. The defense played with plenty of aggressiveness as they had several forced fumbles called back. Regardless, the Steelers’ defense continues to bend more than they break. Grade: B+ Special teams Jarrett Bailey: Chris Boswell was great, going three-of-three on field goals. Pittsburgh can’t seem to go a game without a special teams penalty, was Sean Murphy-Bunting was penalized on a punt, and the Steelers allowed a 42-yard kickoff return. The kick coverage unit is still a problem. Grade: B- Joey Bray: His consistency has been shaky this season, but Chris Boswell nailed all three of his field goals on Sunday. Given the offense’s struggles to punch the ball into the end zone, the Steelers didn’t win yesterday without Boswell. For the second straight week, Kaden Wetjen had a decent return nullified by a penalty. There have been little to no explosive returns for Wetjen this season, but it’s not all his fault considering the Steelers special teams always get in trouble for holding in those situations. Grade: A Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! stories.summary: In a game where violence is the point, the NFL has yet to come up with a satisfactory player safety measure that doesn't legislate the football out of football.
stories.detailText: During Sunday's game against the Houston Texans, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo did what so many hard NFL runners have done before. He took a handoff, burst through a hole and lowered his helmet into an oncoming defender at the second level. The immediate result was a crunching collision, a 7-yard gain and Texans safety M.J. Stewart left reeling on his back. It was an Oklahoma drill in real game action, and Skattebo got the best of it. Holy Cam Skattebo! 🚛 pic.twitter.com/8p0gsxaukg — ΛWTHΞИƬIK (@awthentik) October 25, 2026 But the functional result of the play was not a 7-yard gain for New York. Instead of second-and-3 at the 30-yard line, the Giants were moved back half the distance to the goal for first-and-20 at their their own 13. Skattebo got flagged for unnecessary roughness because he lowered the crown of his helmet directly into Stewart. Skattebo was incensed. As was Giants head coach John Harbaugh, who gave an official an earful on the sideline. 'That's how your'e supposed to run' On Monday, Harbaugh expounded on his thoughts on the penalty, a day after New York's 27-21 win. "Did you see me after the play expressing my opinion? That's how I felt about it." John Harbaugh explains his perspective on Cam Skattebo's personal foul penalty: pic.twitter.com/1uBCxyDpmE — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 26, 2026 "I understand the idea," Harbaugh said of the penalty. "I also understand human physiology and anatomy and the way the body works. Skat runs low. You have to run low. "You have to run low to protect the football. You have to run low to protect your body. You can't run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head's down there too. You can't move your head off your shoulders. It's a physical impossibility. "I'm quite sure Skat's not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a bettering ram. That's not the way he's thinking. He's leading with his shoulder, that's what he's trying to do. He's trying to keep his head in a good, strong upright position. "His pads are down there low. He runs low to the ground. He runs low to the ground. That's a good thing. That's football. That's the way you're supposed to run. That's how you protect yourself and the football." Thus is the crux of the issue. Harbaugh's right. That's football. That's the way Skattebo and other ball carriers have been taught to run since they started playing football at the youth level. That punishing playing style has been celebrated through the history of the game with runners like Earl Campbell, Christian Okoye, Marshawn Lynch and Craig "Ironhead" Heyward the subject of countless highlight clips. Does the NFL have a point? With a flag like the one on Skattebo, the NFL is punishing a football player for playing football. The flip side of the coin is a legitimate concern for player safety and, by proxy, the health of the league. Lowering the crown of one's helmet like Skattebo did is a path to serious injury. Defensive players get thrown out of college games for doing the same thing. And we've all seen a defender get flagged for an injurious hit when it was the ball carrier who put his body in the position to cause the injury by lowering his head in the first place. In flagging Skattebo, the NFL put the culpability of protecting his body and others from injury in his hands. Harbaugh acknowledged that point at the top of his comments Monday. But he concluded with the toughest question for the NFL to answer when it comes to player safety. What exactly is Skattebo supposed to do here? "We haven't heard from the league," Harbaugh continued. "Maybe they'll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it terms of what they want us to teach, and that would be great." Harbaugh's not likely to get an answer anytime soon. In a game where violence is the point, the NFL has yet to come up with a satisfactory player safety measure that doesn't legislate the football out of football.

stories.title: Snap Reactions: All nickel, no base as Seahawks stymie Chiefs
stories.summary: The Seahawks slowed Kenneth Walker and the Chiefs offense in Week 7 with speed, not size.
stories.detailText: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs is tackled by Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks and Josh Jobe #29 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images And just like that the Seattle Seahawks are back. After consecutive losses to the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos had fans in despair at the state of the title defense for the Seahawks, a resounding 20-3 thumping of the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football has changed things. Seattle was far from an offensive juggernaut, but with the defense showing up in midseason form, all the offense needed to do was put points on the board, and that they did. Anthony Bradford played every offensive snap in his return from injured reserve, while Charles Cross missed a dozen snaps after leaving with a high ankle sprain that is expected to keep him out of the lineup for some time. Josh Jones stepped in for Cross, playing more snaps against Kansas City than he had through the first six weeks combined. At running back Emanuel Wilson continued to earn the bulk of the workload in Jadarian Price’s absence, while at tight end Nick Kallerup’s 26 offensive snaps had him on the field more than fellow tight end Eric Saubert and almost as much as receiver Tory Horton. On defense, the Seahawks spent the entire game in nickel, with Julian Love, Nick Emmanwori, Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe and Ty Okada all playing every snap, with Nehemiah Pritchett joining the party for 11 snaps and Trevon Diggs on the field for a half dozen plays after being relegated to the practice squad, but then elevated for the game. For those who might have expected a beefed up defensive front from Mike Macdonald to slow down the running back with the most rushing yards second most rushing yards in the NFL, Jarran Reed and Brandon Pili combined for just 21 snaps. And on special teams there was a slight tweak as well, with Mike Morris finishing with 17 special teams snaps, which put him ahead of Brady Russell by a single snap. Rodney Thomas, Nehemiah Pritchett, Patrick O’Connell, Irv Charles and Jimmy Ciarlo all finished the game in double digits for snaps played on special teams. And now it’s on to another Sunday of football without stressing about the Seahawks, as Seattle will host another primetime game at Lumen Field on Monday Night Football in Week 8 when the Chicago Bears come to town.

stories.title: Panthers put Taylor Moton on injured reserve
stories.summary: Veteran right tackle Taylor Moton's return to the Panthers lineup turned out to be a short-lived one.
stories.detailText: Veteran right tackle Taylor Moton's return to the Panthers lineup turned out to be a short-lived one. Moton was placed on injured reserve on Monday due to the fractured fibula he suffered in Sunday's blowout loss to the Buccaneers. Moton was playing in his second game since being activated from a stint on the non-football injury list that was necessitated by blood clots in his lung during the offseason. First-round pick Monroe Freeling started at right tackle while Moton was out for the first four games of the year and took over after his injury on Sunday. Linebacker Nick Hampton was signed off the practice squad to fill the empty roster spot. Hampton had five tackles on Sunday as a temporary elevation.

stories.title: Giants say Dominic Zvada’s placekicking job is not in jeopardy
stories.summary: John Harbaugh says there will not be a kicker tryout.
stories.detailText: Dominic Zvada (34) after one of his two misses on Sunday. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dominic Zvada’s job as New York Giants placekicker is safe, for the time being. After Zvada, an undrafted rookie, missed kicks of 56 and 44 yards in Sunday’s victory over the Houston Texans, making him just 4 of 9 on field-goal attempts in the last three games, many thought the Giants would at least hold a kicker workout during their bye week to assess their options. “We’re not going to be doing that right now, no,” head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday. Zvada won the job from Ben Sauls with an excellent spring and summer. He went 9 of 9 over the first three games of the season, but went just 2 of 5 in Week 5 against the Washington Commanders and missed both of his field-goal tries vs. the Texans. Harbaugh passed on a 55-yard kick in the third quarter on Sunday after those two misses, punting instead. Harbaugh expressed confidence in Zvada immediately after Sunday’s game. “I think he has to go ahead and pound that thing through straight,” Harbaugh said. “I think he’s doing what a lot of rookies do — just trying to get it through the uprights. I’m not really worried about Zvada. He just has to do it, but I’m totally confident he will because I know how good he is and know what a good head he has.” Zvada knows he has to be better. “I just pushed it,” Zvada said. “It’s unacceptable. Luckily … I’m surrounded by teammates who really support me and keep me ready for the next one. For us to win, that’s great. I’m going to do my thing during the bye to make sure I’m right for when we go to [play] Philly.” Zane Gonzalez (Miami Dolphins), and Jake Moody (Baltimore Ravens) are the only two veteran kickers currently on practice squads. Free agent kickers include 35-year-old Brandon McManus, and 42-year-old Matt Prater. Sauls has not had any reported tryouts since being waived by the Giants with an injury settlement. His injury, and the severity of it, is unknown.

stories.title: Cowboys key matchup: Brian Schottenheimer vs Vic Fangio
stories.summary: The Cowboys need Brian Schottenheimer to be a difference maker tonight
stories.detailText: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images For the first time this season, we will be focusing more on the coaches on the sideline than the players on the field. With the Philadelphia Eagles extremely banged up on offense, and Brian Schottenheimer scooting closer-and-closer to the hot seat, this may be the biggest game of Schottenheimer’s coaching career. The Cowboys head into this week seven matchup fully healthy on offense with the Eagles near full health on defense, minus Nolan Smith out due to a concussion. We have yet to really see it so far this season, but the Cowboys need Schottenheimer to be the “elite play caller” he referred to himself as late last week. Unlike the last two weeks, the Cowboys should expect a pretty clear picture of Vic Fangio’s plan. Like we have learned with Christian Parker, Fangio is not a heavy blitzer and relies on his coverage scheme to keep opposing offenses under control. While we should expect Fangio to ramp up his pressure a bit more due to the Cowboys struggles to handle it the last few weeks, Dak Prescott should not be dealing with as many exotic blitz looks pre-and-post snap like he did against Tampa Bay and Green Bay. The Philadelphia Eagles defense currently looks like a shell of itself from recent years. Through six weeks, the Eagles defense ranks 25th in EPA/play, 23rd in drop back EPA/play, and 31st in rush EPA/play. Given the struggles of the Cowboys running game this season, this is a matchup they can get back on track with. Jalen Carter has turned it on over the last few weeks, after playing with an injured wrist early in the season. Zack Baun is still one of the better linebackers in the NFL, but the depth behind him can be targeted in the running game. With Nolan Smith out tonight, expect the Cowboys to run it early towards AJ Epenesa and/or Arnold Ebikete. With the names like Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, Riq Woolen, and Andrew Mukuba in the secondary, you would think the running game would be the only path to success for the Cowboys offense, but their secondary outside of Mitchell has struggled this year in coverage. Similar to Javonte Williams, this is a solid matchup for the Cowboys wide receivers to get back on track both as pass catchers and run blockers. At the end of the day, this all comes down to Schottenheimer’s ability to prove himself as a play-caller and game-planner. We have not seen much consistency from the Cowboys offensive coaching staff so far this season, but it’s a great week, in a must-win game, to get back on track.

stories.title: Patriots-Bears racks up 19.86 million on Thursday night
stories.summary: The Bears' Thursday night win over the Patriots delivered on the scoreboard that matters most to the NFL — eyeballs.
stories.detailText: The Bears' Thursday night win over the Patriots delivered on the scoreboard that matters most to the NFL — eyeballs. Amazon announced that the Week 7 opener generated 19.86 million viewers on average for Prime Video. It was the second most-watched Thursday night game for Prime Video, behind only the 2025 Christmas night game between the Broncos and Chiefs. It was also the most-watched Week 7 Thursday night game since it became part of the weekly collection of windows. For the season, Prime Video is averaging 17.71 million viewers, a 12-percent increase over last year's average through the first six games of the year. The quality of the matchups is the key. Both teams entered the game 4-2, and both have strong national followings. This week, Prime Video will be hard pressed to match that number, with the 3-3 Panthers visiting the 4-3 Packers. Sure, Cheeseheads will unite to watch their favorite team. With Carolina losing by 30 to the Buccaneers on Sunday, however, Panthers fans may decide to take the night off. But we're getting to the point in the season where games that may have looked good in May won't deliver on the promise, and that other options have emerged as far more compelling games. With Panthers-Packers on Thursday (and with the 2-4 Eagles visiting the 1-4-1 Commanders on Sunday night), the 1:00 p.m. ET window has the 4-3 Ravens at the 5-1 Bills, the 6-0 Vikings at the 4-2 Lions, and the 5-2 Browns at the 5-2 Steelers. Then there's the AFC West showdown at 4:25 p.m. ET between the 5-1 Chiefs and the 5-2 Broncos.

stories.title: Sources: Packers LB Zaire Franklin has hairline fracture in leg
stories.summary: Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin has a hairline fracture in his leg and center Sean Rhyan is believed to have a high ankle sprain, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
stories.detailText: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin is dealing with a leg hairline fracture, while center Sean Rhyan is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Rhyan left Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions with an ankle injury. X-rays were negative, but he is expected to get an MRI on Monday. Rhyan will be expected to miss four to six weeks if imaging shows a high ankle sprain. Not only did the Packers lose Rhyan after just four snaps against the Lions, but they also lost primary backup center Jacob Monk to a quad injury after five snaps. Second-year pro John Williams finished the game, playing the final 58 snaps. Those were the first career regular-season snaps Williams has played on offense. Monk was put on injured reserve with the Packers signing Mekhi Becton to the active roster from the practice squad. Coach Matt LaFleur said after the game that he did not expect Rhyan or Monk to be available for Thursday's game against the Carolina Panthers . Franklin suffered what LaFleur called a shin injury during a collision in practice last Thursday. On Friday, LaFleur said Franklin is not expected to go on injured reserve, meaning the team believes he likely will miss fewer than four games. Although it's his first year with the Packers after arriving in an offseason trade with the Indianapolis Colts , the ninth-year veteran quickly became a key part of the defense. He was elected defensive captain, rare for someone in the first year with a team, and has been the unit's signal-caller. Franklin ranks third on the team in tackles (41) and has two quarterback hits, a forced fumble and a pass breakup. After Franklin's injury, the Packers played without both of their starting inside linebackers. Edgerrin Cooper , who was lost to a torn Achilles in Week 4, will miss the rest of the season. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper played the two inside linebacker spots against the Lions.

stories.title: Packers sign Mekhi Becton to 53-man roster, put Jacob Monk on IR
stories.summary: The Packers had a couple of offensive linemen go down with injuries in Sunday's loss to the Lions and they moved one of them to injured reserve on Monday.
stories.detailText: The Packers had a couple of offensive linemen go down with injuries in Sunday's loss to the Lions and they moved one of them to injured reserve on Monday. Jacob Monk injured his quad after replacing starting center Sean Rhyan in the first quarter of the game. He will now miss at least four games as a result of being shifted to injured reserve. The Packers filled his roster spot by signing veteran guard Mekhi Becton off of their practice squad. Becton signed with the team late last month. Becton started 14 games for the Chargers in 2025, but was released in March. He started 15 games while helping the Eagles to a Super Bowl win in 2024 and spent his first four seasons with the Jets. Rhyan is believed to have a high-ankle sprain, which could also make him an injured reserve candidate. John Williams finished out Sunday's game at center for Green Bay.

stories.title: Recap: Saints play Steelers in inaugural Paris matchup
stories.summary: Catch up on all the action from France.
stories.detailText: PARIS, FRANCE - OCTOBER 25: Devaughn Vele of the New Orleans Saints run with the ball under pressure from Jaquan Brisker of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the NFL game between Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at Stade de France on October 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the first-ever NFL regular-season matchup on French soil, the New Orleans Saints were hoping to make it back-to-back wins for the first time this year as they faced off against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Here’s a recap of everything that went down at the Stade de France. First Quarter The Steelers got the opening drive off to a fast start as Jaylen Warren broke into Saints territory with a 29-yard run. After four more runs, two each from Warren and Rico Dowdle, Aaron Rodgers was incomplete with a pass intended for DK Metcalf on third down. Chris Boswell’s 28-yard chip shot gave Pittsburgh a 3-0 lead. The Saints responded well to begin their opening series, as Tyler Shough found Bryce Lance and Chris Olave for medium gains before converting a third down with a 14-yard pass to Devaughn Vele. But after a run for no gain from Alvin Kamara and a pair of incompletions, the black and gold had to punt. Starting at his own 4-yard line, Rodgers worked his way near midfield with a variety of short throws alongside runs from Warren. Second Quarter After a pair of incompletions, Pittsburgh had to punt. Shough began the ensuing possession with a huge chunk gain, connecting with Barion Brown for a 49-yard pass. Soon after, he found Kendre Miller for 13 more, but was then forced into a 3rd-and-long after taking a sack. Daniel Carlson converted from 38 yards to tie the game. Warren continued to hurt the Saints on the next series, with a 26-yard catch-and-run to begin the drive. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-14, Rodgers found Metcalf for 51 yards to give Pittsburgh 1st-and-goal. Darnell Washington made the catch in the end zone to put the Steelers up 10-3. New Orleans faced 4th down straight away as they looked for a response, which Shough converted on an 11-yard throw to Olave. He then found Vele and Lance before converting another third down with a 13-yard pass to Kamara, who nearly found the end zone. A couple of plays later, on 4th-and-goal, Vele caught the 1-yard touchdown pass to tie the game at 10-10. Rodgers then got to work in the two-minute drill, setting up a 47-yard kick from Boswell to give Pittsburgh a 13-10 halftime lead. Third Quarter New Orleans embarked on a mammoth drive to begin the second half, highlighted by a 24-yard connection from Shough to Vele on a 3rd-and-long. But on the edge of the red zone, Shough’s pass intended for Olave was intercepted by Payton Wilson. Rodgers responded with a long drive of his own, as Pittsburgh moved into Saints territory with Warren continuing to run at will. Brandon Smith caught a 20-yard pass to put the ball in the red zone, but the first sack of the afternoon for the black and gold came at a good time as Chase Young and Carl Granderson were able to force Pittsburgh into a field goal attempt. Boswell was good again from 39 yards. Fourth Quarter Trailing 16-10, New Orleans put together an 11-play, 47-yard drive on which Shough was 7-for-7. But penalties hampered their efforts, and Carlson was soon out to attempt another field goal. He was no good from 52 yards. Pittsburgh proceeded to go three-and-out as Young got to Rodgers again. But the Saints only found one first down on the ensuing series before punting themselves. From there, the Steelers ran down the clock to great effect, with Rodgers scrambling on a 3rd down for the decisive yardage. Boswell came out to convert a 39-yard kick to ice the game, but an offside penalty against the black and gold meant Pittsburgh could kneel out the clock instead to secure a 16-10 victory. The Saints return home after the bye week to play the Cleveland Browns on November 8.

stories.title: Aaron Rodgers was good enough in Paris, but RBs were sublime: Steelers report card
stories.summary: Coach Mike McCarthy's offense managed just one touchdown, but the defense almost completely shut down the New Orleans running game.
stories.detailText: The Pittsburgh Steelers picked up their second international victory in as many years on Sunday, Oct. 25, by beating the New Orleans Saints by a 16-10 margin at Stade de France outside Paris. It was far from the prettiest win of the season. First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s offense managed only one touchdown, and the defense was on its heels at times against the Saints passing game led by quarterback Tyler Shough. Nevertheless, the Steelers continue to lead the AFC North as they head into a crucial divisional rematch against the Cleveland Browns team that beat them on Thursday Night Football in early October. Here’s a look at USA TODAY’s report card on the effort that led to victory in the first NFL regular season game in France. Required reading: Aaron Rodgers calls out NFL owners, wants to see more international games Quarterback - B Aaron Rodgers threw it deep more often than he has the past couple of weeks, to mixed results. He hit receiver DK Metcalf for a 51-yard play that set up the offense’s only touchdown of the day. He later scrambled and found receiver Brandon Smith for an impressive 20-yard conversion. He also overthrew some open receivers, which contributed to the Steelers settling for three field goals on a day that they were otherwise moving the ball well. The short passing game success is great, but you’d like to see him hitting on more of the longer throws than he has been of late. Running backs - A+ Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren accounted for 223 yards from scrimmage against the Saints. Not much more is needed to be said about it than that. These guys are making the most of every touch right now, and Dowdle looks like he might be starting to get as hot as Warren has been in recent weeks now that he’s returned from his Week 2 toe injury. Receivers - B- Were it not for the long catch Metcalf made, it might have been a much more frustrating afternoon for the veteran. He finished with just two catches on six targets. The other catch went for just five yards. Alas, he made the biggest play of the day that put the Steelers in position to win, so he should be credited for that. It was encouraging to see Smith make an important contribution with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson still nursing injuries. And Germie Bernard might have had a better performance were it not for some of the aforementioned overthrows. Tight ends - C Darnell Washington made the most athletic play of the game on his toe-tapping 4-yard touchdown pass from Rodgers in the first half, allowing the quarterback to pass Peyton Manning for third on the NFL’s all-time list for touchdown passes. Unfortunately, that was his only catch. Pat Freiermuth had two catches for 20 yards but dropped a red zone pass in the second half that forced the Steelers to settle for a field goal. Offensive line - B The Saints got to Rodgers for three sacks, but he had plenty of clean pockets to work with, too. Pro Football Focus data registered just six other pressures, all hurries and no QB hits. In the running game, Warren and Dowdle were able to find plenty of holes. The Steelers averaged a robust 4.9 yards per carry as a team and were consistently comfortable with running on third downs, a sign of McCarthy’s belief in his line’s ability to push the opponent around. Defensive line - A The Saints totaled just 18 rushing yards, at a paltry average of 1.1 yards per carry. Seven of those yards came on scrambles from Tyler Shough, a reflection of just how well the Steelers’ were tracking ball carriers. In the passing game, Shough had three passes batted at the line of scrimmage. A little more pressure might have been nice, but the Saints did a nice job of using the Steelers’ offensive tactics against them with short and quick throws that beat the rush. Shough's time to throw was a season-low 2.49 seconds, per PFF. Linebackers - A Payton Wilson came up with a game-changing interception to start the second half, and Patrick Queen nearly had one of his own. Neither was a major liability in the passing game, as Shough increasingly relied on throws toward the sideline. They also had a major part in slowing the New Orleans running game. T.J. Watt added a sack that looked to be a strip and recovery as well at first before replay assist overturned it. Secondary - C+ The degree to which New Orleans became one dimensional offensively is a complicating factor here. The defensive backs were playing basically every snap in coverage by the second half, so it’s not necessarily a damning indictment that some production leaked through. Shough finished the day with completions on 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards. Forty-nine of those yards came on a single pass play to Barion Brown that set up the Saints’ only field goal. Coaching - B- As good as Patrick Graham’s defense was against the run, the interception of Shough to start the second half and Daniel Carlson’s missed 52-yard field goal amounted to major second-half bailouts against a Saints offense that was moving the ball. McCarthy’s offense moved the ball but didn’t produce the points necessary to put this team away long before the Steelers ultimately did.
