stories.summary: Detroit Lions injury updates on Amon-Ra St. Brown and Ennis Rakestraw.
stories.detailText: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-OCTOBER 25: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (14) carries the ball under the pressure of Green Bay Packers safety Xavier McKinney (29) during an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026. (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell gave a couple of injury updates in his Monday afternoon press conference, and it’s mostly good news. Let’s start with Amon-Ra St. Brown. I’m guessing many weren’t aware St. Brown was even dealing with an injury, as he never exited the game and wasn’t given a specific injury designation on Sunday. However, Detroit Football Network’s Justin Rogers noted that the Lions did not make him available in the locker room because he was getting treatment for a swollen ankle . Campbell said they expect to sit St. Brown for Wednesday’s practice, but they’re optimistic he’ll be okay and are hoping he’ll be ready to go for Thursday. “He and Ennis (Rakestraw), I think those guys will probably sit Wednesday, but the plan is to get them going Thursday, and I think that they’ll be fine. They should be good,” Campbell said, before adding. “Now, we’ll see when we get there, but—yep.” St. Brown is coming off his best game of the season, hauling in nine catches for a season-high 153 yards. That’s the fifth-most yards he’s had in a single game for his career. Obviously, missing him would be a big deal, but Campbell doesn’t sound too concerned at the moment. The Lions are expecting the same trajectory for cornerback Ennis Rakestraw, who did leave the game early with an ankle injury. “It’s not major, he’s got a little ankle here,” Campbell said. “We feel like, as of right now, he’ll be at practice on Thursday. That’s kinda what we’re looking at. But we don’t feel like it’s major as of today.” Rakestraw was part of a pretty massive cornerback rotation against the Packers. Rakestraw (21 snaps) shared playing time with D.J. Reed (61), Roger McCreary (67), Rock Ya-Sin (14), and Khalil Dorsey (14). It was a game plan inspired by the Dallas Cowboys’ attack against the Packers to keep the players fresh. Campbell said it’s an approach they will continue to consider moving forward. “I think there was also merit for a number of those guys plays,” Campbell said. “Letting them all kinda play, getting some reps and using them in different situations, different packages.”

stories.title: Eagles activate Landon Dickerson, Grant Calcaterra, Eli Stowers
stories.summary: The Eagles added three players to their active roster ahead of Monday night's game against the Cowboys.
stories.detailText: The Eagles added three players to their active roster ahead of Monday night's game against the Cowboys. Guard Landon Dickerson was activated from injured reserve along with tight ends Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers. Cornerback Jakorian Bennett has also been designated for return, but remains on injured reserve. Dickerson started the opener at left guard, but has been out with a knee injury for the last five games. Calcaterra has been out the whole year with a back injury and Stowers has missed all six games with a quad injury. Stowers was a second-round pick this year, so Monday is set to be his NFL debut. The Eagles also elevated running back Elijah Mitchell and linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby from the practice squad on a temporary basis.

stories.title: NFL insider would be ‘shocked’ if the 49ers don’t make a trade after linking them to 3 pass rushers
stories.summary: NFL insider Jordan Schultz said the 49ers have been conntected to several defensive players
stories.detailText: Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images NFL insider Jordan Schultz appeared on a podcast and discussed two potential teams that could be aggressive at the trade deadline. Schultz went as far as saying he’d be “shocked” if the San Francisco 49ers didn’t make a trade: “I think we’re headed for a very active deadline,” Schultz said. “I think we can see anywhere from 12 to 20 trades—and two teams I’m watching very closely: The 49ers and the Bears. I’ve heard both teams connected to several defensive players, including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack, and DeForest Buckner, along with some names who aren’t necessarily on the trade block. I think both Chicago and San Francisco wanna be aggressive. I’d be shocked if they don’t make a move before the deadline.” The 49ers and Bears, with Caleb Williams under center, are two of the NFC’s top offenses. It makes sense why they’d want to add a pass rusher. In the Niners’ case, they’re 24th in the NFL in pressure rate. One thing the Falcons did well against Kyle Shanahan’s offense was to get pressure with four rushers. It’s something every team strives to do. There’s little reason to think Arizona would help a divisional foe by trading them an asset like Sweat. Mack is in the final year of his contract. The 35-year-old has three sacks, six tackles for loss, and 14 pressures on the season. In Week 4 against the Seahawks, Mack had two tackles for loss, three pressures, and a sack. John Lynch probably made the call to the Chargers after he watched Mack in Week 4. Would it surprise you if the 49ers made multiple trades? Is there a world where they make a move for Mack and Buckner?

stories.title: Patriots re-sign edge rusher Jose Ramirez to practice squad, release offensive lineman
stories.summary: Jose Ramirez spent the preseason with the Eagles before landing in Foxborough.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jose Ramirez #43 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After two weeks away, Jose Ramirez has reclaimed a locker at Gillette Stadium. The New England Patriots officially re-signed the outside linebacker to the practice squad on Monday and released offensive lineman Jacob Rizy to make room among the 17-man group. ESPN’s Mike Reiss and Patriots on SI’s Ethan Hurwitz were first to report the moves heading out of the mini bye. Ramirez, 27, originally landed in head coach Mike Vrabel’s fold after being waived by the Philadelphia Eagles at the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline in August. The 6-foot-2, 252-pound preseason visitor to Foxborough earned a promotion in late September. He checked into two games while on the active roster and recorded one tackle across 30 snaps between defense and special teams. Upon clearing waivers , a return to the practice squad followed in October. So did the edge rusher’s release ahead of what became a 26-19 AFC East win over the New York Jets. Selected in the sixth round of the 2023 draft class at No. 196 overall, Ramirez appeared in four games and notched one quarterback hit while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The former MAC Defensive Player of the Year by way of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan went on to spend part of 2025 with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats and recorded four tackles to go with one sack in three games. He circled back from the CFL to the NFL on a futures contract in January. Rizy, 24, had been brought back on New England’s practice squad after injuries depleted the interior line ahead of last week’s 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears. The 6-foot-5, 306-pound rookie first joined the scout team at its formation and was released midway through September. Signed by the Patriots as part of the organization’s undrafted class of 2026, Rizy played 155 offensive snaps at center through three preseason games before being waived leading up to the NFL’s cutdown deadline. A former second-team and first-team All-Ivy League selection, Rizy spent three years at Harvard and two years at Florida State. He made 27 starts over that span while logging work at center, left guard, right guard and right tackle. A spot remains open on the 53-man roster as a divisional matchup nears. The Miami Dolphins host next Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Hard Rock Stadium.

stories.title: Klint Kubiak: Kirk Cousins is our starting quarterback
stories.summary: Kubiak added that there's "no controversy" at the position.
stories.detailText: There won't be a quarterback change in Las Vegas this week. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak opened his Monday press conference by saying that Kirk Cousins will be the team's starter for their Week 8 game against the Jets. The announcement came a day after Kubiak said the team is " thinking about everything to fix our problems" when asked about turning to rookie Fernando Mendoza. "There is no controversy there," Kubiak said. "He's playing at a very high level. He's gotta continue to do that for us to win and we gotta keep helping all the areas around him. Excited for him to go play against the Jets." Kubiak said that Mendoza is "going to play at some point," but reiterated that Cousins is playing well and that the Raiders are "in the hunt" with a 3-4 record on the season. Cousins was 26-of-44 for 295 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams, but did much of his damage after the Raiders fell behind 28-3 in the first half of the game.

stories.title: How did the Giants spark their running game vs. the Texans?
stories.summary: The backs, the blocking, and the schemes all played a part in the Week 7 success of the running game.
stories.detailText: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo celebrates a touchdown. | Getty Images Life comes at you fast in the NFL. Last week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo was (effectively) benched following a game-changing overtime fumble against the Washington Commanders. He saw just six snaps and zero carries against the New Orleans Saints in what was the second-lowest point of his NFL career. ( Last year’s season-ending ankle injury being the lowest point of his career ) The Giants’ run game as a whole reached a new low after degrading over the three weeks from Week 4 to Week 6, and the Giants’ running backs were averaging just 2.4 yards per carry against the Saints. Fast forward seven days and Skattebo was once again the Giants’ starting running back. He responded to the lesson being conveyed by John Harbaugh by having the best day of his NFL career. The Giants’ running game got off to a bit of a slow start, but they eventually wore the Texans’ defense down and started breaking big runs. Skattebo had carries of 11 yards, 19 yards (4th down), 16 yards (touchdown), and 42 yards to set up Devin Singletary’s game-sealing 30-yard run. All told, Skattebo had 17 carries for 124 yards (7.3 yards per carry) and a touchdown. It was his first 100-yard game as a pro, and by far his most efficient day. Prior to this week, Skattebo hasn’t had a 100-yard performance as a pro and just two games of more than 80 yards. Singletary, meanwhile, had 41 yards and a touchdown on five carries (as well as 14 yards on three catches). The Giants’ running backs totaled 180 yards on the ground in just 28 carries (6.4 yards per carry), with three touchdowns. It would have been even more, except Skattebo also had a 7-yard run called back for unnecessary roughness. #Giants RB Cam Skattebo just absolutely obliterated #Texans S M.J. Stewart—but was called for unnecessary roughness for lowering his helmet. This is not the NFL you grew up watching. pic.twitter.com/6jt8xE4qXP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 25, 2026 So what changed this week? How did the Giants’ running game go from non-existent to game-defining in the span of a week? We’ll start at the macro level and then zoom in. Schemed for success The decision to start J.J. McCarthy was a significant one for the success of the Giants’ running game. The threat of the zone-read or designed quarterback run added a critical element of indecision to the Texans’ defense that the Giants were able to exploit. That was demonstrated perfectly on Tyrone Tracy’s touchdown run. The Giants line up in 12-personnel on the 2-yard line. The condensed formation and short field leads to what is, effectively, a nine-man box while the Giants have just seven blockers on the play side. However, the play is also designed with an extended mesh between McCarthy and Tracy. That mesh creates the potential of a zone-read, which the Giants double down on by releasing Isaiah Likely into a shallow route to the right. ( Played at 1/2 speed ) The Giants run zone blocking to the offensive left, leaving the left defensive end (Jadeveon Clowney) and slot corner (Kamari Lassiter) unblocked on the offensive right. The extended mesh point and Likely’s route combine to freeze Clowney, Lassiter, and FS M.J. Stewart. The Giants’ offensive line does a great job of folding the Texans’ front to the offensive left, while the momentary indecision gives Tracy all the time he needs to get to the second level and across the goal line. Tracy himself shows solid vision to anticipate both his blockers and the defense at the first and second levels, as well as the agility to hug his blockers and find room where the frozen defenders simply can’t reach him. The Giants also made use of formations that, if they’ve used them before, they’ve used them extremely sparingly. Most notably, we saw the Giants align in the Pistol formation — as opposed to the Shotgun — in the second half of the game and use it to great effect. The Pistol is something of a hybrid formation that combines elements of the traditional I formation with the Shotgun formation. Like the I-formation, the running back is several yards behind the quarterback. The quarterback, meanwhile, is 3 to 5 yards behind the center as in the Shotgun. The Pistol combines the advantages of both formations, giving the quarterback the view of the defense he enjoys in the Shotgun, while also giving the running back the runway he typically gets in a traditional I-formation. The Pistol is also highly versatile and can be run as a spread formation with three to four wide receivers, or as a power formation with multiple backs or tight ends. The Giants used the Pistol on Skattebo’s flagged run up above, but perhaps the most notable example of that came on Cam Skattebo’s fantastic 16-yard touchdown run. And in this case, the Giants come out in a very heavy 22-personnel set with two tight ends, as well as fullback Patrick Ricard and Skattebo. The Pistol has a few distinct advantages for a back like Skattebo. While Skattebo doesn’t have much top-end speed, he has impressive acceleration, and the additional separation between him and the line of scrimmage allows him to take the hand-off in stride before continuing to accelerate. The extra two steps allow him to hit the hole that much harder than from the shotgun. Likewise, the extra second gives the Giants’ blockers time to lock in and their blocks develop, creating more defined holes for the back. Notably, there’s time for Chris Manhertz, Ricard, and Jermaine Eluemunor to seal off an alley for Skattebo on the right side, while Isaiah likely gets into position at the second level. The longer runway also gives Skattebo a bit more time and perspective to scan the defense, and better perspective to anticipate defenders at the second and third levels. The Giants probably shouldn’t eliminate the Shotgun formation completely, however using the Pistol at a much higher rate could be a positive development for the running game. The backs: Vision, patience, and physicality Before we talk about the running backs themselves, we need to give a tip of the cap to the Giants’ blockers. Perhaps another week of practice with Brian Hudson as the starting center helped the interior, and perhaps getting Eluemunor back (albeit playing through an injury) made a difference as well. But the Giants’ blocking was some of the best we’ve seen since Week 1. It wasn’t perfect, far from it in some cases, however the Giants maintained a physical edge throughout the game which eventually won out at the end. On top of that, the secondary and perimeter blockers like Malachi Fields, Manhertz, Isaiah Likely, and Ricard all played critical roles in turning merely “okay” runs into successful carries. But turning to the runners themselves, each of the Giants’ backs played with a level of patience that we haven’t seen from them previously. For example, one of the big topics of conversation has been how Skattebo would seek out contact and run full speed into defenders, not allowing blocks to develop or using his vision to find holes. The first play of the game showed Skattebo running with much better tempo and patience behind the line of scrimmage, as well as seeking out his running lane. Notice how Skattebo runs with a “slow to the hole, fast through” tempo, allowing the blocks in front of him to develop before hitting the line of scrimmage. He also does a very good job of using his pathing to pull second level defenders out of their alleys and allow for the blockers at that level to take them out of the intended running lane. Finally, he does a great job of waiting until Eluemunor makes his block to cut back to the right and access the running lane. Ricard isn’t quite able to win the initial leverage battle and is ultimately shed by edge Will Anderson Jr. to stop the run after just 3 yards. However, this run was set up to go much further had the block been sustained for just an instant or two longer. We can’t make the same types of claims about Devin Singletary as we can about Skattebo. While Singletary has never been spectacular in any one facet of his game, he’s at least competent in every area. He has consistently run with good patience and vision, allowing him to make use of his quickness and agility. We got a prime example of this on the final play of the game. It’s worth noting that this is another Pistol run, this time with Ricard in the backfield instead of playing as a tight end. As in the first run of the game, we see Singletary doing a great job of tempoing his run to both give his blockers time to lock in their blocks, and to influence defenders’ angles. He also makes a series of subtle adjustments to his pathing to move defenders just out of position, allowing him to juke them and force poor tackle attempts. From there, Singletary’s contact balance does the rest as he survives incidental contact and glancing blows to find the end zone. Final thoughts It’s notable that the Giants’ run game finally found traction and ignited against one of the NFL’s best run defenses. The Texans’ defense isn’t what we’ve come to expect from them over the previous two years, and they’re definitely feeling the absence of S Jalen Pitre. However, they still had the third-ranked run defense (83 yards per game allowed), and their defense has been hurt much more by explosive passing plays than gashed by the run. Of course, the Giants had explosive passing plays as well, with McCarthy hitting six explosive passes on nine attempts of more than 15 yards downfield. That vertical passing stresses the defense, forcing them to pick their poison. Nevertheless, the Giants’ offense responded and rebounded after woeful performances against the Commanders and Saints. The blocking was significantly improved (though, again, far from perfect), and the backs did a much better job of making the most of what was blocked for them. The coaching staff did their job in putting the players in position to succeed, and John Harbaugh pulled the correct lever in starting McCarthy. Now the Giants go into a much-needed bye week. The question is whether they can maintain the momentum and build upon their performance against the Texans as they get healthier between now and their November 8th game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The next step for them will be to continue to find down-to-down consistency, and perhaps a healthier Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor, as well as a more settled McCarthy, will help lead to that consistency. If so, the Giants’ performance in Week 7 was a great starting point and exactly what the team needed.

Brown missed last week’s game with a knee injury he suffered agains the Jets. Vrabel also noted that the team will have to make a decision on offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, whose 21-day activation window from injured reserve closes this week. Meanwhile, offensive guard Greg Van Roten and safety Dell Pettus could return to practice this week as they work their way back from injured reserve. The Patriots will continue managing their injured reserve list for the rest of the season, with just six return designations remaining. “The depth that you have at the position or the need and I don’t think it’s something that you really want to make a habit of but we’re in the position that we are,” Vrabel said of managing it. “So kind of figuring out, one who’s healthy. who’s healthy enough to return. Some guys aren’t and then we’ll see where we go with the depth at each position.” On the practice field Monday, the Patriots managed the workload of several veterans as they were without Rhamondre Stevenson, Marcus Jones, Dre’Mont Jones, Christian Elliss, Robert Spillane, Kevin Byard, Hunter Henry and Morgan Moses.

stories.title: Buffalo Bills open as slight favorites over Baltimore Ravens in Week 8
stories.summary: The Buffalo Bills and Josh Allen renew their rivalry with the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8
stories.detailText: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 07: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills carries the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter at Highmark Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are back in action for Week 8 after a bye that proved fruitful for their overall standing in both the AFC East and the AFC in general. Following a two-game west coast road stand where they picked up wins against the Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders, the Bills are back in Orchard Park, NY and ready to welcome the Baltimore Ravens at the new Highmark Stadium. At 5-1, Buffalo now shares a piece of first place in the AFC, while Baltimore is stuck in the AFC North basement with a 4-3 record. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook expect a close game, with the Bills currently 3.5-point favorites (-3.5) over the Ravens . Buffalo’s defense has struggled to stop opposing offenses in most games to this point in the season, and Baltimore just gave up 35 points to the Cincinnati Bengals. Could we see a high-scoring affair this coming Sunday? The current odds don’t expect a track meet, with the over/under set at O/U 53.5. It’s going to be important to be tuned-in to both teams’ injury throughout the week. Of significance for the Bills is whether or not wide receiver DJ Moore (AC joint sprain) and defensive tackle Ed Oliver (hip) are healthy enough to suit up in Week 8. The Ravens’ biggest concerns continues to be the health of quarterback Lamar Jackson, who has missed the last three games due to a high ankle sprain. This will be the 15th game in the all-time series between Buffalo and (the current) Baltimore, with each team having won 7 games in that span. The Bills and quarterback Josh Allen are 4-3 against the Ravens since 2018, which includes a pair of playoff wins. Buffalo and Baltimore last sparred in primetime during Week 1 of the 2025 NFL season. The Bills pulled off an incredible comeback win late in the fourth quarter set in motion by Ed Oliver’s forced fumble of running back Derrick Henry. With just over four minutes left, Allen got to work in guiding Buffalo’s offense to 16 unanswered points and a 41-40 win to start the season. stories.title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy praises jumbo package, OL Spencer Anderson
stories.summary: Expect more jumbo packages from the Pittsburgh offense moving forward.
stories.detailText: Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images | Getty Images In a callback to the Steelers’ 2025 offense under Arthur Smith, Pittsburgh broke out its six-offensive-lineman package versus the Saints on Sunday. And in a 16-10 win where the Steelers out-rushed New Orleans 148 yards to 18, it’s fair to say the decision paid off. Like last year, utility offensive lineman Spencer Anderson served as the extra blocker in the jumbo package, playing 13 snaps on Sunday. Twelve of those were run plays, and per Steelers writer Tom Mead , the results on those rushes were 77 yards, 6.4 yards per carry and three runs over nine or more yards. Speaking to the media on Monday, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said the Steelers’ jumbo package success in 2025 “absolutely” played a role in its return in 2026. “When you get the job, the first thing you do, you sit and down and starting going through the personnel,” McCarthy said. “And Spencer (Anderson), I was so impressed with him and it was a big part of the discussion of how we were trying to forecast him for where we felt he could play, because he played so many positions.” McCarthy compared Anderson to current Bills and former Cowboys lineman Conner McGovern, saying he can play every role from center to guard to fullback: “We gotta get him on the field,” McCarthy said. “When you have someone like Spencer with his unique talents, it gives you such great versatility,” he added. McCarthy hinted that part of why the jumbo package didn’t play a major role in the Steelers’ game plan until Week 7 was because the Steelers first gave Anderson the starting right guard role to open the season. Then, Anderson dealt with a bone chip in his right leg in late September. “In fairness to (Anderson), I wanted to give him a chance to compete for a job, and that’s why we started the way we did with him at right guard, and then he had the injury and so forth,” McCarthy said. Despite free agent signing Brock Hoffman having secured the starting right guard spot moving forward, McCarthy indicated that the Steelers still want to find ways to get Anderson on the field. “(Anderson) carries a lot of value on our football team, especially up front,” the Pittsburgh head coach said, “and it’s important for us to continue to create opportunities for him.”

stories.title: Packers kicker Trey Smack adds two more misses to uninspiring start
stories.summary: The Packers’ rookie kicker is off to a worse start than the last kicker the Packers drafted.
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Trey Smack #28 of the Green Bay Packers lines up a field goal during the fourth quarter of a game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Among many other reasons, the Packers lost to the Detroit Lions on Sunday because they couldn’t put two short field goals through the uprights. 2026 draft pick Trey Smack missed outright from 26 yards, then had a 35-yard attempt blocked on the Packers’ final drive. In a game the Packers lost 20-17, you don’t have to be a math major to see how things could have played out differently. The Packers spent three (admittedly very late) draft picks to get Smack, trading their final two picks in this spring’s draft to move up to select him with the 216th pick. He was the only kicker drafted this spring and, so far, he’s been one of the worst kickers in the NFL. In an era where kickers are making more of their attempts than ever, Smack lags far behind the field. The league average field goal percentage this season is 84.2%, but Smack has made just 68.8% (11 out of 16) of his attempts. Not all of those misses are his fault; two of his field goal attempts this year have been blocked, and those still count against his overall percentage. But even if Smack had converted those two blocks, he’d still be below the league average this year. Worse, it’s where he’s missing that’s concerning. Smack can’t seem to make field goals from an area of the field that are all but a sure thing for most kickers. All five of Smack’s misses have come from 49 yards or less; he’s nine of 14 (64.3%) from that distance this season. Among the five total kickers this season who have made less than 70% of their field goals this year, only Smack and Harrison Mevis have multiple misses from under 49 yards. Mevis, you’ll note, is currently out of a job. His two misses against the Buffalo Bills in Week 5 were enough to cost the Rams the game and earn him his walking papers. And it’s worth noting that Mevis made all 14 of his PATs while with the Rams this year. Smack is 13 of 15 in that department, and his miss against the Vikings in Week 1 played a big role in how that game played out down the stretch. Smack is off to an even worse start than the last kicker the Packers drafted. Anders Carlson’s misses from 43 and 45 yards cost the Packers dearly in losses to the Raiders (19-17) and Giants (24-22) in the 2023 regular season, and his late miss against the 49ers in the playoffs (from 41 yards) changed San Francisco’s final drive from a game-tying effort to a game-winning one. But on the whole, Carlson’s stats look downright desirable. He finished his rookie year converting 29 of 36 field goals (80.1%) counting the playoffs and hit 83.9% of his kicks from 49 yards and in. If Smack hits at that clip, the Packers’ season might look a whole lot different. Smack still has a job for now, and 16 field goal attempts is hardly a big enough sample size to judge a rookie kicker. Things could still improve. But it’s hardly an inspiring start, and it leaves the kicking game as just one more thing the Packers need to improve as they try to keep their season on track.

teamStories.title: Fernando Mendoza’s time will have to wait — Raiders staying put at QB
Klint Kubiak says Kirk Cousins will remain Raiders' QB1 over Fernando Mendoza
teamStories.summary: Klint Kubiak announced his plans to stick with Kirk Cousins as the starter for Week 8, shutting the door on any quarterback controversy.
teamStories.detailText: Kirk Cousins is here to stay. The Las Vegas Raiders appeared to have somewhat of a quarterback controversy on their hands heading into Week 8. In the midst of a four-game losing streak, Vegas could've opted to turn to the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Fernando Mendoza , as the starter going forward. Mendoza's time will have to wait for now. Head coach Klint Kubiak shut the door and left no doubt about the starting quarterback job when he met with reporters on Oct. 26. "Kirk is our starting quarterback," Kubiak said. "There is no controversy there. He is playing at a very high level and he's gotta continue to do that for us to win." It was a decision that came not even 24 hours after Kubiak opened the door for some debate about who would line up under center. "I think at this point, we’re thinking about everything," Kubiak told reporters, via Vegas Sports Today, after the Raiders lost to the Los Angeles Rams 35-21 on Sunday, Oct. 25. "How to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter. Personnel, scheme, we’ve got to talk about all of it." However, the timing wasn't right to make the switch. "Eventually, Fernando is going to play football," Kubiak said on Oct. 26. "We have a plan. We don't have a timeline for that." "Fernando is gonna play at some point. It's not gonna be this week." The coach wanted leave no doubt about the state of the position in an effort to send a message to the team. "He's the leader of the team," Kubiak said. "The guy that touches the ball on every play so it's important that the team knows where we're going." Kubiak noted that it will be his decision when and if that switch is made at quarterback. teamStories.title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
teamStories.summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
teamStories.detailText: Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams after a blockbuster trade in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players -- Von Miller (No. 9), Cameron Jordan (No. 17), Calais Campbell (No. 25), T.J. Watt (No. 26), Danielle Hunter (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack (T-29th) -- in the top 30. Joining the top 30 soon could be Aaron Donald , who unretired to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th. As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. Miller, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him. But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's. As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. Week 7 update Hunter and Watt were the only ones to record sacks this week, with Hunter jumping back over Campbell in the rankings. Week 6 update With Garrett still out, it was another quiet week on the sack front. Of the active leaders, it was the oldest that recorded the lone sack of the week in Campbell. He moved back in front of Hunter. Week 5 update Hunter was the only player among the active leaders to record a sack this week, moving him ahead of Campbell to No. 26 all-time. Hunter now has three sacks through five games. Week 4 update Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR. Week 3 update There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season. Week 2 update The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. Donald (33rd) made his season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. Week 1 update Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee. After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

teamStories.title: Kirk Cousins to remain Raiders' starting QB vs. Jets, Klint Kubiak says
teamStories.summary: Kirk Cousins will remain the Raiders' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Jets, coach Klint Kubiak announced Monday.
teamStories.detailText: HENDERSON, Nev. -- Kirk Cousins will remain the Las Vegas Raiders ' starting quarterback for this Sunday's road matchup against the New York Jets , and "there's no controversy" about sitting the 38-year-old veteran for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza , coach Klint Kubiak said Monday. "[Cousins is] playing at a very high level, and he's got to continue to do that for us to win," Kubiak said. "We got to keep helping all the areas around him. [I'm] excited for him to go play against the Jets." Cousins' job security appeared to be in question when Kubiak said he would evaluate "everything," including the quarterback position, after the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, which extended their losing streak to four games and dropped their record to 3-4. Cousins has been the least of the Raiders' troubles during their losing streak. He leads the NFL in touchdown passes (16) and is third in passing yards (1,877). Cousins overcame a shaky first-half performance against the Rams and finished with 295 passing yards and two touchdowns. He had a 59.1% completion rate and a passer rating of 94.4. Los Angeles blitzed Cousins on 29.2% of his dropbacks, and he was sacked twice and pressured 19 times. Kubiak said Mendoza is "going to play football." Mendoza made his NFL debut at the six-minute mark of the fourth quarter in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots , completing 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards in his short time on the field. Kubiak added that the team has a plan for Mendoza, but they don't have a timeline for when the Heisman Trophy winner will make his first career start. As of now, Cousins has the full support of Kubiak. "Kirk is playing really well, and we're in the hunt," Kubiak said. "It's really important that we keep playing really well behind him and keep developing Fernando. "Fernando is going to play at some point. It's not going to be this week."

It is my read that Kubiak was never really going to consider a quarterback change this week, but his big-picture way of answering the question Sunday night fueled the speculation.
